summary: This note is a broad history of the Space Race between the United States and the Soviet Union, from early satellite and crewed-flight milestones through Apollo 11's 1969 Moon landing. It also covers Soviet programs such as Vostok, Soyuz, and Salyut, the use of captured German rocket specialists, the founding of Project Mercury, and the Soviet motives behind the rivalry.
one_line: A history of the US-Soviet Space Race, from Sputnik and early crewed flights to the Apollo 11 Moon landing and later Soviet space stations.
key_facts: Apollo 11 landed safely in the Pacific Ocean on July 24, 1969.
The Apollo 11 mission was completed with 161 days to spare before the end of the decade set by Kennedy's commitment to land a man on the Moon.
The USSR finally canceled its N1 rocket in 1976, after two more launch failures in 1971 and 1972.
Vostok 6 carried Valentina Tereshkova into space on June 16, 1963, making her the first woman in space and the first civilian in space.
The USSR did not open its cosmonaut corps to women again until 1980, two years after the United States opened its astronaut corps to women.
The Space Race began on August 2, 1955, when the Soviet Union responded to a US announcement of plans to launch satellites for the International Geophysical Year.
The Soviet Union launched Sputnik 1 into orbit on October 4, 1957.
Yuri Gagarin became the first human in space on April 12, 1961.
Soyuz 3 was launched on October 26, 1968, and cosmonaut Georgy Beregovoy got within 40 meters of Soyuz 2 but could not dock after expending 90 percent of his maneuvering fuel.
The first Soviet docking of spacecraft was achieved in January 1969 by the Soyuz 4 and Soyuz 5 missions.
Korolev reverse-engineered the A-4 rocket with help from Helmut Groettrup's group and built his own version, the R-1, in 1948.
The captured German rocket specialists were repatriated in 1951-53.
NASA transferred the US Air Force's Man in Space Soonest program to the civilian agency, renaming it Project Mercury on November 26, 1958.
On May 5, 1961, Alan Shepard became the first American in space, flying Freedom 7 on Mercury-Redstone 3.

On September 20, 1963, President Kennedy proposed at the United Nations General Assembly that the United States and the Soviet Union join forces to reach the Moon, a proposal Soviet Premier Nikita Khrushchev initially rejected.

entities.name: Apollo 11
entities.role: Mission that landed safely in the Pacific Ocean on July 24, 1969, after the US landed the first humans on the Moon

entities.name: Kennedy
entities.role: US president whose commitment to land a man on the Moon before the end of the decade set the Apollo timeline; proposed joint US-Soviet lunar efforts in 1963

entities.name: Soviet Union
entities.role: Rival state in the Space Race that launched Sputnik 1, Gagarin's flight, and the Vostok and Soyuz programs

entities.name: NASA
entities.role: Civilian US space agency that took over the Man in Space Soonest program and ran Project Mercury

entities.name: N1 rocket
entities.role: Soviet rocket the USSR tried to perfect before canceling it in 1976

entities.name: Vostok 6
entities.role: Spacecraft that carried Valentina Tereshkova, the first woman in space, on June 16, 1963

entities.name: Valentina Tereshkova
entities.role: First woman and first civilian in space, flown on Vostok 6

entities.name: Korolev
entities.role: Soviet designer who reverse-engineered the A-4 and built the R-1; reportedly proposed launching a woman

entities.name: Sputnik 1
entities.role: Satellite the Soviet Union orbited on October 4, 1957, beating the US to orbit

entities.name: Yuri Gagarin
entities.role: First human in space, on April 12, 1961

entities.name: Soyuz 3
entities.role: Piloted mission launched October 26, 1968 to rendezvous and dock with the unpiloted Soyuz 2

entities.name: Georgy Beregovoy
entities.role: Cosmonaut who flew Soyuz 3 and got within 40 meters of Soyuz 2 without docking

entities.name: Soyuz 4 and Soyuz 5
entities.role: Missions that achieved the first Soviet docking of spacecraft in January 1969

entities.name: Helmut Groettrup
entities.role: German rocket specialist whose group helped Korolev reverse-engineer the A-4

entities.name: Gorodomlya Island
entities.role: Lake Seliger island where Soviet officials moved most captured German rocket specialists

entities.name: Project Mercury
entities.role: NASA crewed spaceflight program renamed from Man in Space Soonest on November 26, 1958

entities.name: Alan Shepard
entities.role: First American in space, flying Freedom 7 on May 5, 1961

entities.name: Freedom 7
entities.role: Spacecraft Alan Shepard named and flew on Mercury-Redstone 3

entities.name: Nikita Khrushchev
entities.role: Soviet Premier who initially rejected Kennedy's proposal for joint Moon efforts

entities.name: Gherman Titov
entities.role: First Soviet cosmonaut to exercise manual control of his Vostok 2 craft, on August 6, 1961

entities.name: Stalin
entities.role: Soviet leader who in 1947 ordered development of intercontinental ballistic missiles to counter the perceived American threat

entities.name: Space Shuttle
entities.role: Reusable US orbital spacecraft developed in the 1970s

entities.name: Mir
entities.role: Soviet space station supported by Soyuz spacecraft, later part of the Shuttle-Mir Program with the United States

entities.name: Buran program
entities.role: Soviet program to develop its own large space shuttle

entities.name: International Space Station
entities.role: Space station on which the United States and Russia later worked together
